STAGE 3 — FINAL ANSWER (this record stands alone).
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
ARGUMENT:
(1) geometry_necessity and novelty both go to cocond-markov-poincare-ot. CURVCELL-SID's curvature enters only as a per-code scalar divisor on one distance, d_B(eps,c)/s[l][k] with s=sqrt(kappa), which is a per-prototype bandwidth that a matched Euclidean control (per-code weighted squared distance, standard bandwidth k-means) reproduces exactly — rubric level 2, not 4/5. It is also the family the ledger has already measured: E12 of SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ already proposed free per-prefix curvature c_p in (0.1,10), and E6 measured every curved arm below its Euclidean control (successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, successor_entropy 0.05122 versus l1_br_euclid 0.06207 and resample 0.06363), so CURVCELL-SID is a routine variation of a measured negative. cocond-markov-poincare-ot moves the assignment plan itself — an entropic-OT plan with a Poincare ground cost, diffused by the training transition matrix, with an Einstein-midpoint codebook — and no arm in E6 touched the plan (every arm is a loss, a resampling, or a capacity change), while its own NOVELTY argues that removing behaviour changes the plan and the barycenter weights and removing curvature changes the cost kernel and the mean operator.
(2) downstream_mechanism and behaviour_evidence favour cocond-markov-poincare-ot. It names the affected assignment (j*(i)=argmax_j P_ij), the observables and the direction, and binds them to measured statistics with coverage: E6 gold-prefix survival at depth 2/3 of 0.829/0.161 on 57,439 test rows, and E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 against a permuted null of 0.067, which is the exact headroom the mechanism claims to move. CURVCELL-SID has a sign gap: its formula log(1+B)/[(d-1)R] gives high-branching codes a larger s and therefore larger cells, coarsening precisely the residual region it says must separate eight behavioural branches; it self-admits that the rescaled distance is not a metric and cells may be empty; and E8 (K=16 0.3106 versus K=256 0.0822) attributes the co-location loss to capacity/K rather than to curvature budget, so its behavioural premise is one inferential step removed.
(3) implementability is the one dimension CURVCELL-SID wins clearly: it is fully specified, no gradient flows into s, the refresh schedule and clamp are given, and its cost checks out (1023*256*4 = 1.05M extra multiplies per step). cocond-markov-poincare-ot leaves alpha and q as "measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS)" with no SAFEGUARDS text present, so it loses implementability points; but that is 10 percent of the rubric against a 20+20 percent loss on geometry and novelty, and its cost is separately verified affordable because E10 gives mean out-degree 5.4526, making the sparse products about 3*(5.45*1024*256)*3 = 13M MACs per forward.
FAILURE RISK: the three Sinkhorn sweeps interleave the Markov step with the column-marginal projection onto q, so if alpha is small or the projection cancels the diffusion, cocond-markov-poincare-ot degrades to plain Poincare-cost Sinkhorn — the curved arm E6 already measured at 0.05500, below the 0.06207 Euclidean control — and its own stated risk that B_bt is near the identity (E10's 5.45 mean out-degree over 118,315 edges on a large catalogue) makes that collapse likely; with a single seed and A's own admission that seed noise cannot be separated from mechanism failure, a null result would be uninformative. If the missing alpha/q definition forces a redesign, CURVCELL-SID's frictionless 2-4 percent implementation could return a usable answer while cocond-markov-poincare-ot stalls.
Scores used: cocond-markov-poincare-ot 4/3/4/4/3/3/4 = 3.60; CURVCELL-SID 3/2/2/3/3/4/3 = 2.70.

STAGE: A (cocond-markov-poincare-ot) audit: behaviour direction, geometry, implementability hole
GOAL: check that A targets the defect the evidence actually measures, and find the weakest link.
READ: E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067, source item_sids), E6 (gold prefix alive 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068 at depth 1/2/3/4; target SID inside 20 beams 0.0678), E7 (l1_br per-position NLL 0.00/0.00/0.00/9.03), E10 (edges 118315, distinct_edges 115582, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, edge_density 5.3266, coverage note: sampled users only), E12 (kappa=-1 Poincare ball, exp/log, Mobius addition, Klein Einstein barycentre).
OBSERVED: A's defect statement matches the measured shape exactly: prefix agreement is barely above a permutation null (0.0907 vs 0.067), and ALL of the prefix survival is lost at the last level (1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068) with T4 NLL 9.03. A's mechanism changes the argmax of the plan itself, which is the object that sets those tokens, so the SID hypothesis follows from the statistic with coverage on 57,439 test rows.
GEOMETRY: A has two load-bearing curved operations - Poincare ground cost inside the Sinkhorn kernel and the closed-form Klein/Einstein weighted barycentre as the codebook update - and the barycentre has no Euclidean-mean equivalent, so it is not a glued-on name. But A never specifies a matched Euclidean counterpart (Euclidean-cost Sinkhorn with the same diffusion, Euclidean weighted mean), so it cannot reach geometry 5; ~3.
IMPLEMENTABILITY HOLE: step (4) uses B_bt, a B x B batch matrix, and step (5)-(6) use a usage prior q and an alpha that the text says are "measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS)" - but SAFEGUARDS is not in the bundle. That is an implementability and behaviour defect, not a fatal one - fixable by using the full item set or successor-in-batch restriction, but not specified.
OPEN: nothing further; the comparison is decidable.

STAGE: final tally and decision

B = behaviour 3, geometry 4, novelty 2, downstream 4, falsifiability 4, implementability 4, exploration 3 -> weighted 3.35. DECISION: WINNER cocond-markov-poincare-ot; FIRST LISTED cocond-markov-poincare-ot.
